boundary.description: All tracked project source, tests, docs, configuration, scripts, deploy specs, web assets, and RSI backlogs/scenarios inside the repository root, plus any newly created untracked in-scope files. Derived build caches, VCS internals, third-party installed dependencies, ephemeral agent runtime files, local editor swap files, and secrets/credentials are explicitly excluded and never counted as covered.

exclusions.reason: Git internal object store and repository metadata are never feature artifacts.
Cargo build outputs are derived and rebuildable from source.
Installed third-party frontend packages are external dependencies, not authored project files.
pnpm content-addressable package store is a local dependency cache.
Compiled frontend bundle is derived build output.
Ephemeral agent execution markers and exit files are runtime state, not project deliverables.
Local coding-engine runtime state and worktrees are excluded from project coverage.
Ephemeral RSI gate owner lease and runtime state (gitignored) are not authored project artifacts.
Root deploy marker (the 41-byte commit id written by deploy/controller.sh into a deployed controller tree) is runtime state, not an authored project artifact.
Environment secret files are never indexed or associated in the feature registry.
Environment secret variants are never indexed or associated in the feature registry.
Host environment files (such as spawn.env) hold secrets and are excluded.
Private key material is never indexed in feature coverage.
PEM key/certificate files are excluded from feature coverage.
GPG-encrypted secrets and backup artifacts are excluded from feature coverage.
Dedicated secrets directories are never crawled or indexed.
macOS Finder metadata files are transient local artifacts.
Editor swap files are transient local artifacts.
Secondary editor swap files are transient local artifacts.
Editor tilde backup files are transient local artifacts.
Rust formatter backup files (gitignored) are transient local artifacts.
Transient Cargo.lock backup file (gitignored) is outside project coverage.
Runtime log files are transient diagnostic outputs.
Temporary scratch files are outside durable project coverage.
Partial transfer/download files are transient artifacts.
Tool caches are derived and rebuildable.
Python bytecode caches are derived build artifacts.

features.title: Agent Grading: grading catalog, onboarding exams, routing & calibration
features.summary: Graded presets (`grading_presets`, the fold of the control session's `grading.recorded` events, outside the control fold) mapped to a `ModelProfile`, offline onboarding exams (`evals/onboarding/`), minimum-sufficient task routing by `TaskDifficulty` with a quality-rejection rework step-up (`task.rerouted`) and a fallback to `--model default` for unflagged assignments the catalog cannot cover, and integer-only calibration over quality outcomes read from `mission_tasks` (`spawn grade`, `spawn task assign --difficulty/--preset`). Phase 2: a deterministic brief difficulty classifier for unflagged ephemeral assignments (recorded on `task.assigned` as `classification`), gate `rejected` verdicts stepping rework up in the verdict's own statement, the fleet loop's periodic grading upkeep with an anti-starvation re-probe, and named execution profiles beyond `default|cheap` (`execution_profile`, `/api/grading`).

features.title: Fleet Node Registry, Heartbeats & Drain
features.summary: Owned machines as fleet nodes (M7 #555): `spawn node add|list|probe|drain|undrain|remove`, the heartbeat worker, tcp/udp transports with multi-hop relays and upward registration (`spawn node serve|register`, issue 85), the global E2E-encrypted mesh of issue 87 (Ed25519 node identities, spawn-e2e-v1 sealed envelopes, AEAD-sealed tcp/udp wire, a pure sync WebSocket+TLS client and server, `spawn node coord|connect` with a recursive coordinator tree, STUN/punch and blind relays), the PostgreSQL node store and the Fleet page's node rows. Issue 91 P1a: macOS (Darwin) inventory and heartbeat, battery/AC power telemetry and the low-battery soft drain (`SPAWN_NODE_LOW_BATTERY_PCT`). spawn-node v1 (design §§2–3, §7; PR S2): the shared `spawn-node-proto` crate (signed request envelope and response, size caps, strict JSON, the heartbeat/spec/grant/result/enroll bodies, `tree_sha256_v1` behind `integrate/inputs.rs::scenarios_sha256`) and its golden fixtures `testdata/node-protocol-v1/` (Probe P6). PR S3: the synchronous `spawn-node-gateway` binary (std-only HTTP/1.1, restricted `spawn_node_gateway` login, verify-then-commit `spawn_node_gw_*` calls, 120 s key cache, per-source/per-node pacing, signed responses and grants, streamed results, ranged artifacts) and the protocol text `docs/node-protocol-v1.md`. PR S4 (M2): `integrate/remote.rs` (content-addressed artifacts for the gateway: delta/baseline git bundles, the deterministic controller pack, the registry manifest; the grant env as GATE_ENV minus node-owned names and any database URL; enqueue, lease wait and `take_local` fallback; a stored node result read back into `gate.rs::decide` and routed by the §6.2 outcomes matrix with strikes, exclusion, degraded and the poison-pill refund; the nodes' sweep from the integrator's pass), the `SPAWN_GATE_SHADOW_NODE=1` shadow source beside the runner's (`task.shadow_gated` with `runner: node:<name>`), and `nodes/v1.rs` (`spawn node enroll-token|revoke`, `list|drain|undrain` over P1 and v1 nodes). PR S5 (M3a/M3b): the primary remote gate behind `SPAWN_GATE_REMOTE=node` (inert when unset or `local`, refused otherwise): `remote.rs::Primary` publishes and queues a task's candidate gate as a `gate` job, waits `SPAWN_REMOTE_QUEUE_WAIT_SECS` for a lease and judges locally only when its fenced `take_local` wins; a node's exit-0 acceptance on the job's own five inputs is the task's verdict (M3a, `env.runner` `node:<name>`), its rejection is judged again here unless `SPAWN_GATE_REMOTE_BELIEVE_REJECT=1` (M3b); every other §6.2 outcome is settled on the ledger alone and falls back to the local gate (fallback_local), never an abort, host fault or no_room of the task; a gate on a red main (`SPAWN_GATE_BASE_CHECK`) is never queued and runs locally; an urgent owner landing discards a waiting judging and takes its queued job back; a predecessor's queued gate jobs are taken back at the first pass (`integrate/remote_primary_tests.rs`).

features.title: Dashboard: Live Stream, Master Control, Approvals, Digest & PWA Shell (issue 91 P1a backend, P1b web)
features.summary: The Rust backend of the issue 91 dashboard: `GET /api/stream` (Server-Sent Events on slots of their own, one `LISTEN spawn_events` listener, Last-Event-ID / ?after= catch-up), `POST /api/master/message` (`spawn_human_master_message`: a message to the supervisor that auto-wakes it, in auto/steer/queue/restart modes), the no-ACP approval detector `GET /api/approvals` with its one-click `POST /api/approvals/<session_id>/act` (named keys, the digits of numbered prompts included), and the token-saving `GET /api/context/digest`. The web side (P1b): `web/src/stream.ts` reads `/api/stream` with fetch() and a ReadableStream (the bearer header, never a token in the URL), resumes with Last-Event-ID / ?after=, handles ready and resync, reconnects with jittered backoff, catches up when the page shows again, and is shared among tabs by a Web Lock and a BroadcastChannel (each tab alone without them); its events invalidate Home's polls. Home shows the approvals queue (`approvals.ts`, ApprovalsQueue: one click per answer with approval_id and Idempotency-Key, probed first), Master Control (`master.ts`, MasterComposer: auto/steer/queue/restart with an IndexedDB offline outbox `outbox.ts` that replays idempotently, in memory without IndexedDB) and the digest (`digest.ts`, DigestPanel). Nodes show their power and low-battery soft drain. A dependency-free PWA shell (manifest, icon and a service worker that never caches /api/* or tokens) is embedded in the binary (`serve/pwa.rs`, `web/src/pwa/`) and served by `spawn serve` itself, no-cache. Answers carry the option clicked (`choice_id`), which the server presses and no other; keys for an approval are pressed only while it shows.
